paragraph: Mother! So noble and so god fearing is Dasaratha, that he is the image of dharma. When such a man is alive, how can you say you will follow me into the forest? Never shall I sacrifice my duty, even if it be to inherit the earth, nor shall I accept an inheritance which is not impeccably just. In a life so impermanent, I do not wish to rule a world equally impermanent for which I have little use. The rewards of kingship are so paltry and inferior, compared to the immortal fame gained by strict adherence to righteousness. Rama then bade an affectionate and reverential farewell to his mother.
Situation/Problem_Faced: Rama is consoling his mother, Kausalya, who is emotionally distressed and wishes to accompany him into exile. He reaffirms his commitment to dharma, even in the face of suffering and loss, rejecting any unjust inheritance or impermanent rewards.
Key_Teaching/Action_Taken: Rama highlights the supremacy of righteousness over material gain. He declines the idea of ruling a kingdom won through injustice and comforts his mother by stressing the higher value of dharma and renunciation.
Outcome/Resolution: In this segment, Rama successfully reaffirms his commitment to Dharma and his father's command, firmly but affectionately dissuading Kausalya from joining him in exile. He offers her philosophical comfort and a clear articulation of his moral stance, leading to her ultimate acceptance and his departure.

Mental_Health_Theme_Synonyms.stress Management: Mindful composure, Ethical calm, Detachment under pressure
Mental_Health_Theme_Synonyms.emotional Regulation: Empathic firmness, Loving detachment, Graceful emotional balance

Spiritual_Psychological_Concept_Indian.Concept: Dharma (Righteousness - Rama's unswerving commitment to moral duty)
Vairagya (Detachment - Rejection of worldly pleasures and power)
Satya (Truth - Honesty in action and intention, refusing unjust gains)
Shraddha (Faith - Unshakeable trust in righteousness and the path of duty)

Brief_Summary_Spiritual: Rama exemplifies dharma by rejecting kingship gained through injustice, shows vairagya by detaching from worldly ambitions, and reflects satya and shraddha through his moral clarity and deep spiritual conviction.
Brief_Summary_Psychological: Rama models emotional maturity, ethical consistency, and resilience. By prioritizing principle over comfort, he demonstrates values-based living and compassionate strength in guiding his grieving mother.
